newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker welcomes end to Lufthansa Cargo surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Schenker welcomes end to Lufthansa Cargo surcharges.

text.p: All airlines will follow the lead of Lufthansa Cargo AG and drop their cargo fuel surcharges, a leading German forwarder forecast.
Jochen Smoktun, Schenker International vice-president airfreight Germany, said he expected other airlines to copy the move of the market leader quickly.
Lufthansa Cargo, the airfreight arm of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, announced earlier it would drop its 10 US cents per kg fuel surcharge from April 15.
Fuel prices had now returned to the level of July 1996 and a rise was not expected in the summer, the airline said in a statement.
Smoktun told Reuters: "This is certainly good news because we as forwarders have had problems with clients who did not want to pay the surcharge."
Companies with long-term projects had found it particularly difficult to incorporate the cargo fuel surcharge into their airfreight costs, he pointed out.
Smoktun forecast: "All the other airlines will now follow."
He described the introduction of the surcharge last November at three days' notice as an "outrage".
Lufthansa Cargo is the largest of the four airlines which have announced they will drop their air cargo fuel surcharges.

As the largest international airfreight carrier, the Lufthansa Cargo decision is likely to have a strong influence on the decisions of airlines such as KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, Air France and British Airways.
Delta Air Lines dropped its surcharge on March 13, Virgin Atlantic Cargo followed on April 1 and United Airlines scrapped its charge on April 7.
Lufthansa Cargo first introduced a surcharge of 15 pfennigs per kg, then roughly equivalent to 10 US cents, on November 1 at three days' notice due to spiralling jet fuel prices.
The move was followed by airlines on both air cargo rates and passenger fares in most world markets.
But pressure has been growing from air cargo shippers and freight forwarders on airlines to drop the surcharge in recent weeks.

On April 3, the European Air Shippers Council (EASC) called on airlines to scrap the surcharge on the grounds it could no longer be justified. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax:5017
